definition: How close repeated measured values of a quantity are to each other; recording a reading to the right precision means giving it to the smallest step you can read on the instrument, no more and no fewer figures.
The reading an instrument gives when the true value is zero; subtract it from every reading to get the true values (subtracting a negative zero error adds its size).
A measurement is repeatable if you get the same or a very similar value when you measure it again in the same way and in the same conditions, during one experiment.
A measurement is reproducible if a similar value is found by another method, in other conditions, or in a separate experiment.
